page.title: tinyactors: like SQLite, but for actors
page.description: tinyactors runs statecharts as actors inside your process. Agents can read them, simulate them and check them.

hero.headline: Like SQLite, but for actors.
hero.lede: tinyactors is an actor runtime you link into your program. Each actor is a statechart. No server, no threads, no I/O of its own.

section.heading: An actor is a statechart.
section.p: States, events and timers, written in SCXML. This one charges a card and retries twice.

claim.p: A host is a library. It runs your actors on your event loop, in Node.js, Bun, Python, the browser or C.
An idle actor takes about 1.2 KB in Node.js. The C core takes no memory you did not give it.
Idle actors hibernate to your store and wake on their next event. Two million run with a thousand in memory.

section.heading: Built for agents.
section.p: A coding agent changes a chart the way it changes a function: with all of the behavior in view.

item.text: An actor's behavior is one chart. An agent reads one file, not a call graph.
Charts do no I/O. Every effect is an event to a handler you write.
Outages, retries and timeouts run on a simulated clock, in milliseconds.

section.heading: Simulate a thousand runs.
section.p: A seed decides when the service answers. The clock jumps from timeout to timeout.

example.caption: Change attempts < 3 to attempts < 4 and seed 10 fails.

section.heading: Kill your unit tests.
section.p: A unit test checks one run. A property checks every run a generator can make, and a failure shrinks to the smallest run that breaks it.

claim.p: SCXML defines what every transition does. tinyactors passes all 191 automatic tests of the W3C suite.
Each step an actor takes is traced: the event, the transitions, the states it entered.

section.heading: Build a team chat.
section.p: Five steps, each a program you can run.

item.text: One actor, and a handler for the screens.
Each user is offline, active or away.
One actor decides which rooms exist.
A thousand users, fifty in memory.
Idle actors go to your store and come back on their next event.
Running actors move to a new version of their chart.
The whole host as one blob: actors, timers and clock.
Traces, logs and metrics as OpenTelemetry.
